## What it is

The cradle `screen_wedge` sits in, so the screen stands at `tilt` (45° by default) against
a vertical surface the base is plaqued against — the back face drops straight down from
the ridge to the floor, always. A hollow wedge box printed **fond on the bed**, empty
seen from above, with the electronics
under the screen. The wedge is not fastened to it: it slides down between two rails
onto two pins and is held by its own weight. **The wedge is also the lid**, and the
only way in. Two side panels close over its full 19.6 mm thickness and press-fit onto
`wedge_width`, hiding the USB-C openings `screen_wedge` cuts into its own border.

About **2 h 16 m and 93 g** on the A1 Mini, and it holds roughly 5300× the screen's
weight — this part is nowhere near its strength limit, see below.

## Design notes

- **Why this exists at all.** `screen_wedge` cannot be printed in one piece with its
  own support. Laid on a 60° seat the monolith gives **17 findings, 13 of them
  blocking**: 2 849.9 mm² of 60° overhang, a 107 mm bridge over 1 652.2 mm² which is
  the pocket ceiling the module fits against, a 74 mm bridge over 111.0 mm², and 8
  regions whose first layer starts in mid-air. The two constraints are exclusive: the
  seat wants 60°, the pocket and its walls want ≤ 45°. There is no compromise angle.
  Both reference designs found online split the same way — Waveshare's own is a case
  plus a separate stand, octopint is four screwed panels.
- **`backing` is the parameter, and the ridge height is computed from it.**
  `north_height = seat_height + backing·sin(tilt)`. Backing is how much of the wedge's
  77.8 mm actually lies on the slope, and it is the number with meaning: at **77.8 the
  whole wedge is backed**, so a press anywhere on the glass is pure compression into
  the slope. 63.5 backs only the touchscreen, and below that the top of the active area
  overhangs the ridge, where a **2.46 N** press rocks the screen off its seat — inside
  the range of a firm touch. `reject` guards both ends of that range.
- **Why the ridge is not a parameter.** Any two of {ridge height, tilt, backing} fix the
  third, and the ridge is the one nobody chooses on purpose. As a free number it drifted
  silently: raising `seat_height` 10 mm cut backing to 66.3 mm unless you also raised the
  ridge, and `screen_assembly`'s `tilt` slider — which passes tilt down but never passed
  a ridge height — swung backing from **95.3 mm at 45° to 69.8 mm at 75°** with nothing
  in the viewer saying so. Computed from `backing`, both sliders leave the screen's
  support alone.
- **The lip is the wedge's thickness, 19.60 mm, measured perpendicular to the seat.**
  That is what makes it flush with the glass: it hides no part of the module, whose
  own bottom bezel is 9.09 mm anyway.
- **The lip is never a full-width plate.** As a plate its underside is a 30° downward
  face over **2 470 mm²**. It lives on the side walls and on two ergots, each a solid
  triangle standing on the floor whose own underside falls at 49.7°.
- **The rebate is what stops the screen moving sideways during the slide.** Each side
  wall is a 4 mm shelf whose top lies on the seat, for the wedge's border to rest on,
  plus a 2 mm rail standing 3 mm proud of it. `channel_fit` 0.4 leaves 0.2 mm a side —
  loose on purpose, so the wedge still slides freely down onto the pins.
- **The side panels are a separate job: hiding the USB-C openings, not the slide fit.**
  `rail_height` (3 mm) only ever had to stop sideways play; `screen_wedge`'s own
  border is 19.6 mm thick, so above the rail its USB-C/UART channel openings were
  exposed straight out the side. `side_panel_depth` (19.6, the wedge's full thickness)
  closes over them, and `side_panel_fit` (−0.1mm total) is measured off `wedge_width`
  itself rather than the loose `channel_fit`, so the wedge presses into the last bit of
  its travel instead of rattling.
- **The panel follows the wedge's own back corner exactly, flush — it is not chamfered.**
  That corner reads as a sharp near-90° peak standing proud of the ridge, but cutting a
  chamfer into it there recedes the panel behind the wedge, which fills right up to
  the same corner: tried, and it opened a visible triangular gap along the join instead
  of softening anything. `screen_wedge` drops the polish chamfer on its own outer rim
  perimeter (`on_outer_rim`) for the same reason, so the two land flush with no reveal
  either side of the join. `seating()` also excludes this face's edges from polish here,
  same as the seat and lip planes.
- **Neither the panel's inner (mating) face nor the shelf's inner face is chamfered —
  both are faces the wedge presses or rests flush against, and a bevel anywhere on
  their perimeter breaks that line.** `on_flat_face(edge, x)` excludes any edge lying
  flat on a face perpendicular to X at `±x`, used for the panel's inner face at
  `press_half` and the shelf's inner face at `channel_half - shelf_width`, rather than
  naming individual edges on either. An earlier version (`on_panel_return`) only
  targeted the ridge-return edge by checking `on_plane(edge, ridge, up)` restricted to
  that X — it missed the longer edge running from the front wall's crest up to the
  ridge, which is not one of the profile's named points but an edge the boolean union
  creates there; that one kept its chamfer and showed as a diagonal bevel band down
  the whole inner face. The same gap existed on the shelf's own inner edge, where the
  wedge's border actually lands. Checking the X-plane directly instead of guessing at
  each edge's shape catches the whole perimeter of either face in one test, including
  edges no per-edge check anticipated. The notch relief is handled separately,
  unaffected: it's still built before the panel is added, so the cut never nicks the
  panel's own face.
- **The foot pins run along the slope, not normal to it.** Along the slope they lean
  30° off vertical, so their own underside sits at 60° and prints support-free. Normal
  to the seat they would lean 60° and overhang at 30°.
- **The base is plaqued against a vertical surface**, so the back face drops straight
  down from the ridge (90° at the bottom-right corner in side view). There used to be
  a `footing` parameter for a free-standing desk version with a sloped back face, but
  it was never used — removed 2026-09-04, see Don't.
- **There is no notch relief cut.** An earlier version had one — 0.5 mm square along the
  notch line, meant as the doctrine's inside-corner relief at a load-bearing junction —
  but its box shared an exact X boundary with the rail's inner face at `channel_half`,
  and that tangency tessellated into a visible glitch at the seam once the panel's own
  inner chamfer stopped covering it (see the polish notes above and the changelog). The
  wedge's own bottom-rear edge sits on the bed in its print pose, so polish never
  touches it there and it comes out sharp regardless; nothing was actually perching on
  the corner. Removing the cut settled the glitch and dropped the part's two
  previously-accepted slivers to zero.
- **The back opening is a hexagon, not a circle, because only the roof of a
  horizontal hole overhangs.** Flat bottom and flat sides print as ordinary walls;
  only the last few millimetres closing over the top are a bridge. `back_opening_chamfer`
  (6 mm default) cuts just the top two corners at 45°, leaving a 4 mm flat top —
  short enough to bridge clean — instead of a full-width 16 mm ceiling. The bottom two
  corners stay square: nothing overhangs on the way down, so cutting them would only
  lose bearing area for no printability gain.
- **The opening's position is anchored off the base's own geometry, not fixed
  numbers.** `back_opening_from_left` is measured off the base's left edge
  (`-outer_half`, which moves with `wedge_width`/`channel_fit`/`rail_width`), and
  `back_opening_below_top` off `north_height`, the ridge — the actual top of the back
  face, not the (usually lower) front-wall crest. Both `reject` if the opening would
  run past the back face's own width or height.
- **Nothing the wedge touches is chamfered.** `seating()` pulls every edge lying on the
  seat plane or the lip plane out of the polish pass, because a 1 mm chamfer there is
  1 mm of daylight under the screen. Every other edge keeps its 1 mm chamfer.
- **Breaking is nowhere close either way.** `nurb stress` gives ~5300× margin and
  0.0002 mm of sag.
- **Three cable-tie rings stand off the back face's own interior side**, reusing
  `system.py`'s `anti_tirage_ns` — the same shape `boitier_ps` uses on its own
  north wall, called the same way (`toward_plus_y=False`, projecting into the
  box's interior). Centred on the magnet wells' own X (`outer_half/3`): two on
  the right-hand well's column (`cable_tie_low_z` 15mm, `cable_tie_right_high_z`
  40mm) and one lone ring on the left-hand well's column (`cable_tie_left_z`
  40mm) — raised from the shared 25mm/30mm it started at so it clears the
  magnet well's own boss, which stands off the same wall higher up.
- **The two ramped magnets slide in through a coin slot cut into the
  exterior back face, not a bore.** A round hole drilled straight into the
  ramp face is printed lying on its side (axis horizontal), which overhangs
  past 45° at its own top — same problem `straight_magnet_*`'s
  `puit_couche` solves below, but here there's no system.py helper for a
  slot, so it's built directly via a shared `ramp_magnet_well(x0)` closure
  (called once per side, so both wells can't drift apart in dimensions):
  the mouth sits on the exterior back face (`max_y`), dropped below the
  ridge (`north_height`), and the cut runs straight down-and-in at 45°
  (`-up`: both Y and Z decrease together) until `magnet_wall` of material is
  left before it would break out through the boss's *other* ramp (A→B) near
  its own peak — found by intersecting the ray with that ramp's line. The
  slot's own walls are flat planes at the ramp's angle, so nothing
  overhangs, and no edge in it is chamfered (`on_magnet_slot`, matched by
  each slot's own bounding box). The magnet ends up in the same place a
  round bore would have put it, just entered from above instead of the side.
- **The Z-drop for the slot's mouth is `magnet_cover·√2`, not
  `magnet_cover`.** The slot's top face ends up parallel to the ramp it
  stops short of (both contain X and the fixed 45° "up" direction), but a
  straight drop in Z isn't normal to that ramp — projected onto it, a
  `magnet_cover` drop only closes the gap by `magnet_cover/√2`. Dropping
  `magnet_cover·√2` in Z instead gives a true `magnet_cover`-thick skin
  there. Caught by `nurb check` at exactly the predicted 0.42mm
  (`0.6/√2`) before the fix.
- **`well_width` carries a fixed `+0.9mm` on top of `magnet_diameter + 2·magnet_wall`,
  and it exists only to keep the two magnets aligned with `screen_wedge`'s own,
  unrelated to how tightly the disc actually needs wrapping.** The coin slot
  stops against the boss's *first* ramp (A→B), which faces the open interior
  cavity, not the *second* ramp (B→C, parallel to the seat) the old round bore
  used — so the magnet's own facing direction changed with the slot redesign.
  Enlarging `well_width` grows the whole triangular boss (`ramp`/`climb` both
  scale with it), which walks the A→B intersection point diagonally until it
  lines back up with `screen_wedge`'s hardcoded `magnet_x`/`magnet_y`. Found
  by measuring both magnets' actual built positions (bounding boxes of the
  wedge's `petit_puit` cavity and the base's slot end-cap, both transformed
  into the same frame) rather than by re-deriving the geometry analytically —
  a hand-derived perpendicular-offset estimate got the wrong answer here.
  `cable_tie_left_z` dropped 40 → 37 alongside it: the bigger boss now
  reaches lower, into where that ring used to sit clear.
- `seat_height` is the room under the screen for the electronics. Because the
  ridge rises with it, depth is unchanged —
  `depth = 19.6·sin(tilt) + backing·cos(tilt)` does not mention it.
- **The ergots' underside is flat at Z=0, not tapered to a point.** Below `seat_height`
  ≈ 14 mm at the default 45° tilt, the old taper (straight from the seat point down to
  the origin) fell past 45° and needed support. A 4th polygon point at `(seat_y, 0.0)`
  squares the bottom off instead, so the ergot sits flush on the floor with no
  overhang at any `seat_height`, including 5.

- **A third magnet, `straight_magnet_*`, bores through the back face on a
  horizontal (lying) axis instead of the 45° ramp the other two stand on.**
  It plaques the base against an external magnetic surface, the role
  `base_pesage`'s now-removed `aimant_paroi` used to play (see that file's
  history). A round hole printed with its axis lying flat overhangs past
  45° at its own top, so the cutter is `system.py`'s `puit_couche` (the
  teardrop/"goutte" roof), not a plain cylinder — `puit_debout`'s round
  pad+cutter is for a floor-standing well, axis vertical, and doesn't apply
  here. The pad is a plain box: only the sliver of it that protrudes past
  the plain `wall` (`straight_magnet_cover + straight_magnet_height -
  wall`) is unsupported underneath, short enough to bridge. The magnet is
  pushed in from the interior — the mouth, where `puit_couche`'s own entry
  chamfer sits — and travels toward the exterior, stopping
  `straight_magnet_cover` short of it. Positioned at
  `straight_magnet_from_right` from the base's right edge, at the same Z as
  the back opening's centre (the leftmost feature on this face).

## Don't

- **Don't start the coin slot at the boss's own ridge (its exposed tip).**
  Tried twice: first with the slot cutting from there toward the old bore's
  target point, then with a box aligned to "up" — both left the slot too
  small/oddly placed relative to the boss and, in one pass, blew a huge hole
  through unrelated geometry when the length calc was wrong (66→then back to
  74mm overall height). The mouth is on the **exterior back face**
  (`max_y`), not the boss.
- **Don't compute the slot's stop point from the old bore's target.** The
  right stop is the *first ramp* the slot would break out through
  (`A→B`, computed as a ray/line intersection), minus `magnet_wall` — not a
  fixed offset from the second ramp's midpoint, which was the old bore's own
  logic and doesn't apply to a slot entering from a different face.
- **Don't centre the slot box on its own mouth line.** `Align.CENTER` on the
  thickness axis put half the box above the intended top edge, eating into
  the ramp's own thin top skin. `Align.MAX` hangs the box below the mouth
  line instead.
- **Don't drop the slot's mouth by `magnet_cover` in Z and assume that's the
  skin thickness left behind.** It isn't — see the note above. A `nurb
  check` finding that lands at a suspiciously exact fraction of a parameter
  (0.42mm = 0.6/√2) is usually a projection, not a bug in the value itself.
- **Don't assume a `nurb check` finding reported once means only one of two
  symmetric wells has the problem.** Checked directly: both wells' faces
  match to the sub-micron, before and after polish. The checker reports one
  instance of a duplicate finding, not all of them.

- **Don't put `straight_magnet_from_right` at 10mm.** Tried: the well's own
  margin (`MARGE_PUIT`) comes within 0.3mm of the shelf's inner face
  (`channel_half - shelf_width`, 59.25mm) — under the printer's 0.6mm
  reliable minimum, plus 4 sliver faces at the tangency. 15mm clears it.
- **Don't chamfer the straight magnet well's own boss frame** (the box's two
  faces perpendicular to X, at `straight_magnet_x ± straight_magnet_half`).
  It sits flush against the plain back wall; a chamfer there tessellates a
  sliver at the tangency, same failure mode as the ramped wells' own end
  faces (see `on_magnet_well`).
- **Don't use `puit_debout` for a well bored into a vertical wall.** It's a
  floor-standing well (axis vertical, printed as a plain ring — no overhang).
  Wrapping it in a `Plane` to point its axis horizontal still leaves a round
  cutter and a round pad, and a round hole/boss lying on its side overhangs
  past 45° at the top. Tried first, looked plausible, `nurb check` didn't
  catch it — `puit_couche` is the one built for a lying axis.
- **Don't bring back `footing`/`footing_edge`.** Removed 2026-09-04: the base is
  always plaqued against a vertical surface in practice, the free-standing desk
  version was never printed, and the parameter drifted the back face's own angle
  independently of `tilt` (see the old changelog entries below, from before removal).
- **Don't merge this back into `screen_wedge`.** The monolith is 13 blocking findings,
  and the supports land inside the pocket on the module's 0.5 mm fit surface and across
  the four M2.5 counterbores, which end up bored at 30° to the bed.
- **Don't make the lip a full-width plate** "so the screen bears evenly". It is a 30°
  downward face over 2 470 mm². The ergots exist for exactly this reason.
- **Don't put pins normal to the seat**, at the top corners or anywhere. Tried: 2 fails
  at 22 mm² each of 30° overhang, and there is nothing under them to corbel onto. The
  rebate does that job with no holes in the wedge at all.
- **Don't add a transverse wall under the ridge.** It was in for one revision. Measured
  against no wall at all: 0.019 mm of sag versus 0.017, margin 305× versus 307× — **2 %**
  — and it blocks component placement and cable runs. The shear panel that keeps an
  open-top shell square is the wedge itself, once seated.
- **Don't make the side profile a V or a tent.** The wedge would slide off. The lip and
  the low front wall are what catch it.
- **Don't reach for magnets for the slide fit, the sideways play, locating, or
  rocking** — the lip, the rails, the pins and full backing already do those jobs.
  This isn't a blanket ban on magnets any more: two small ones now sit near the
  ridge, flush with the seat plane, for a different job (see below). Magnets never
  helped tipping either, only against a magnetic support.
- **Don't chamfer the magnet wells' hole rims or their boss end-faces.** Tried
  without the exclusion: the default 1mm chamfer on the hole rim and on the boss's
  X-bound end faces ate into `magnet_wall` (1.6mm by design, sized tight around the
  5mm magnet), dropping the wall there to 0.67mm — under the printer's 1.00mm
  reliable minimum. `on_magnet_well()` pulls both out of the polish pass, same
  pattern as `seating()`'s exclusions.
- **The magnet wells run through to the exterior back face; `magnet_cover` (0.6mm)
  is what's left on the seat side, on purpose.** The magnet is pushed in from
  behind, so only a thin membrane needs to stand between it and the wedge for it
  to still act through the plastic. That membrane is well under the printer's
  1.00mm reliable minimum, so `min_wall = 0.6` in this card's settings tells
  `nurb check` that 0.6mm here is accepted, not a defect — same mechanism as a
  sliver count, just for a wall.
- **The bore's overcut is sized off its own radius, not off `wall`.** The hole
  meets the exterior face at 45°, so its flat end cap only fully clears the face
  once it overshoots by about the hole's radius; a `+wall` (2mm) overcut left a
  0.17mm sliver where the cap's far edge hadn't broken through yet. `+magnet_diameter`
  clears it with margin.
- **Don't chamfer the seat slope or the lip face**, and don't "fix" the sharp edges they
  leave. They are the faces the screen lies on.
- **Don't bring `north_height` back as a parameter.** It was one until 2026-08-21 and it
  drifted every time `seat_height` or `tilt` moved, silently changing what holds the
  screen up. `backing` says the same thing in the units that matter and the ridge falls
  out of it.
- **Don't tighten the pin fit.** 5.5 mm sockets on 5 mm pins is a free fit on purpose:
  two pins 60 mm apart on two separately printed parts will not meet a snug fit.
- **Don't chamfer the side panels' top-back corner** where they meet the wedge, even
  though it looks like a sharp spike. Tried, at 8 mm: it opened a visible triangular
  gap along the join because the wedge fills right up to that same corner and the
  panel no longer reached it. Fix any pointedness there on `screen_wedge`'s own edge
  instead, matching what `on_outer_rim` already does — never on the panel's face.
- **Don't bring the notch relief cut back**, at `channel_half`, at `press_half`, or
  widened by a small overlap epsilon — all three were tried. Sized to `channel_half`
  it sat exactly tangent with the rail's inner face and tessellated into a visible
  glitch at the seam; resized to `press_half` the same tangency just moved into the
  shelf's own body instead; widened by 0.1 mm past `channel_half` it still left the
  same sub-mm² tangent slivers, only shifted. Nothing was perching on the corner
  without it — the wedge's bottom-rear edge sits on the bed in its own print pose, so
  polish never touched that edge either way. Removing the cut entirely is what
  actually cleared it.
- **Don't turn the 16mm back opening's corner cut into a plain square.** Tried
  2026-09-05 while chasing "no chamfer": a plain square roof there is a 60°
  ceiling and `nurb inspect` flagged it. `back_opening_chamfer` stays — what
  the user meant by "no chamfer" was `polish`'s 1mm edge break on the
  opening's rim, not this bridge-relief cut. `on_back_opening` excludes both
  openings' rims from `polish`'s `keep` set instead; a plate covers both once
  the box is mounted, so neither rim needs breaking.
- **Don't give the second opening (6×6mm, at `second_opening_offset_x` from
  the first) a corner-relief shape.** At 6mm its own roof bridges clean with
  no overhang finding — the plain-square cut only failed on the 16mm one.

## Changelog

- 2026-09-04: `screen_assembly`'s two magnets realigned after the coin-slot
  change — `well_width` +0.9mm (grows the boss, walking the slot's stop
  point back toward `screen_wedge`'s hardcoded position) and
  `cable_tie_left_z` 40 → 37 (the bigger boss now reaches lower). Found via
  `screen_assembly`: the two parts' magnet cavities, measured in the same
  assembled frame, no longer overlapped after the coin-slot redesign.
  Checks clean on both `screen_base` and `screen_assembly`.

- 2026-09-04: coin slot geometry fixed twice more after the first cut.
  (1) The slot box was centred on its own mouth line (`Align.CENTER`),
  which let half of it eat into the ramp's own top skin — now `Align.MAX`
  hangs it below that line. (2) The mouth's Z-drop below the ridge was
  `magnet_cover` (0.6mm), which `nurb check` caught as a 0.42mm section —
  exactly `magnet_cover/√2`, since the drop isn't normal to the ramp the
  slot stops short of. Fixed to `magnet_cover·√2`. Also: both wells now
  built by one `ramp_magnet_well(x0)` closure instead of a loop with
  externally-shared variables, and `on_magnet_slot` added so nothing in
  the slot gets chamfered. 147 faces, checks clean.
- 2026-09-04: the two ramped magnets' round bore replaced by a coin slot,
  `magnet_slot_gap` (2.2mm) added. Mouth on the exterior back face,
  `magnet_cover` below the ridge; runs down-and-in at 45° (`-up`) until
  `magnet_wall` of material is left before breaking out through the boss's
  other ramp (found via ray/line intersection with that ramp's edge). A
  round hole bored into the ramp face is printed lying on its side and
  overhangs past 45° at its own top, same failure mode `straight_magnet_*`
  solves with `puit_couche`. 143 → 151 faces, checks clean.

- 2026-09-04: third magnet well added, `straight_magnet_*`, bored through
  the back face on a horizontal axis (`system.py`'s `puit_couche`, teardrop
  roof) rather than the 45° ramp the other two stand on — plaques the base
  against an external magnetic surface. First tried with `puit_debout`
  (round pad+cutter, meant for a floor-standing well); replaced once it was
  clear a round hole/boss lying on its side overhangs past 45° at the top.
  `straight_magnet_from_right` moved 10 → 15mm after `nurb check` flagged
  the well's margin coming within 0.3mm of the shelf's inner face at 10mm.
  133 → 143 faces, checks clean.
- 2026-09-04: `magnet_diameter`'s default raised 5.0 → **5.2mm**, now sourced
  from `system.py`'s new `PETIT_PUIT_DIAMETRE` — at 5.0 the magnets would not
  seat, no clearance on a 5mm disc. This well stays its own custom shape (an
  angled ramp cut into the sloped back face), unlike `screen_wedge`'s flat
  well which now calls `system.py`'s `petit_puit` directly; only the diameter
  constant is shared.
- 2026-09-04: cable-tie rings' upper Z split into `cable_tie_right_high_z`
  (30mm, unchanged) and `cable_tie_left_z` (its own ring, raised 25 → 40mm)
  so the lone left ring could move independently — 40mm clears the magnet
  well's own boss on that wall, which starts at 46.4mm; 45mm would have hit it.
- 2026-09-04: `footing`/`footing_edge` removed. The base is plaqued against a
  vertical surface unconditionally now; the free-standing desk version they
  enabled was never printed. `depth` is just `north_y`, the back wall is a
  plain vertical box, and the cable-tie rings' own footing=0 `reject` is gone
  with them.
- 2026-09-04: cable-tie rings' shared upper Z (25 → 30mm).
- 2026-09-04: three cable-tie rings added on the back face's interior side,
  `system.py`'s `anti_tirage_ns` reused from `boitier_ps`. Two under the
  right-hand magnet well's X (`cable_tie_low_z` 15mm, `cable_tie_high_z`
  25mm), one under the left-hand well's X at 25mm. 66 → 118 faces, checks

- 2026-09-04: magnet well axis moved 1mm down-slope from the ramp face's exact

- 2026-09-04: magnet wells extended through to the exterior back face, so each

- 2026-09-04: two magnet wells added, near the top of the back face (the one
  with the port), centred at 1/3 and 2/3 of the base's width. Each is a
  triangular boss standing off the back wall's interior face: a 45° ramp away
  from the wall then a 45° ramp back to it, so the second ramp's face lands
  parallel to the seat plane (at the default 45° tilt) — a `magnet_diameter`
  (5mm) × `magnet_depth` (2mm) hole is cut into that face, `magnet_wall` (1.6mm)
  thick around it, so a magnet glued in sits flush under `screen_wedge`'s
  underside once the wedge is seated. Needed `on_magnet_well()` to keep the
  polish pass off the hole rim and the boss's end faces — see Don't. 56 → 64
  faces, checks clean.
- 2026-09-04: back opening added — a 16 × 16 mm hexagonal port through the back
  face, centred 25 mm from the left edge and 40 mm below the top of the back face
  (the ridge, `north_height`, not the front-wall crest). Hexagonal rather than round:
  flat bottom and sides, top two corners cut 45° (`back_opening_chamfer` 6 mm) so
  only a 4 mm flat top has to bridge instead of a full-width ceiling. 42 → 56 faces,
  checks clean.
- 2026-09-04: `seat_height` 30 → 5. The ergot's underside squared off flat at Z=0
  (a 4th point added to the `lip` polygon) instead of tapering to the origin, which
  at 5 mm fell to a 19.8° ramp — 70° off vertical, well past the 45° overhang limit.
  Flat-based ergots have no overhang at any `seat_height`. 130.50 × 68.87 × 98.87 →
  130.50 × 68.87 × 73.87 mm, 66.4k mm3 (−34.7%), 42 → 44 faces, checks clean.
- 2026-09-04: notch relief cut (`fit`) removed entirely, and the parameter with it.
  It sat exactly tangent with the rail's inner face at `channel_half`, and once the
  panel's own inner chamfer stopped masking that seam (previous entry), the tangency
  showed as a visible glitch at the notch. Widening the cut by a small overlap epsilon
  only moved the same sub-mm² tangent slivers rather than removing them; dropping the
  cut did. 52 → 42 faces, checks clean, zero slivers — the 2 previously accepted are
  gone. `screen_assembly`'s stale `tilt` default (60°, from before `screen_base`'s own
  default moved to 45°) fixed to match in the same pass.
- 2026-09-04: `on_flat_face(edge, x)` now also excludes the shelf's inner face
  (`channel_half - shelf_width`) from polish, matching the panel's. Same bug as the
  panel below: nothing had named the shelf's own inner edge, so it kept a chamfer
  where the wedge's border actually lands.
- 2026-09-04: `on_panel_return` replaced by `on_panel_inner` (later generalised to
  `on_flat_face`), which excludes the panel's whole inner face (`X = ±press_half`)
  from polish instead of naming the ridge-return edge alone. The narrower check missed
  a diagonal edge from the front wall's crest up to the ridge — not one of the
  profile's named points, so it never matched `on_plane(edge, ridge, up)` — and it
  kept its chamfer, showing as a visible bevel band running the height of each inner
  panel face. 64 → 60 faces.
- 2026-09-04: two more internal edges dropped from the polish pass — the panel's
  return to the ridge (`on_panel_return`) and, by reordering the notch relief cut
  before the panels are added instead of after, the panel's mating face no longer
  gets nicked by that cut either. Both were chamfers with no purpose, on faces a
  square box slides against; the first one also opened a visible gap along the
  wedge join. Traded for 2 accepted sub-mm² slivers where the relief cut and the
  rail's inner face sit exactly tangent — see `[accepted]` above.
- 2026-09-04: two side panels added, closing over `screen_wedge`'s full 19.6 mm
  thickness (`side_panel_depth`) and press-fitting onto `wedge_width`

  the back face now drops straight from the ridge for mounting against a vertical

- 2026-08-21: `north_height` replaced by `backing` (77.8, the whole wedge), with the

- 2026-08-21: `seat_height` 20 → 30 for more room under the screen, and `north_height`
